requirementChecks.criteria: Read the original file properties: Format: presentation document; at least eight actual pages. Stage: final.

Compare all visible identity and wardrobe features with the supplied identity sheet and record, allowing only framing, pose and natural occlusion. Preserve the mature face, center-parted gray bob, brown eyes, left-cheek mole, rolled indigo sleeves, single-square-pocket rust apron, charcoal trousers, brown lace-up boots and no jewelry. P05, D02, D04 and E05 must show right-handed operation of the walnut-handled curved hook knife; D05 must show right-handed shaping with the pale ash-handled straight knife. Changed identity, wardrobe, tool construction or handedness fails. Film evidence is assessed separately by whole-file review.

Verify that P01-V is the central 2:3 crop of the P01 photographic exposure, with identical pose, spoon, grain, shadows and room details. Both show Nora at the bench holding the finished spoon and carry both required strings. Assess publication-crops.png against the 360 × 240 mm spread, 3 mm outer bleed, central 160 × 240 mm crop and fold at 180 mm. The face, both hands and complete spoon must clear the fold by 12 mm and the relevant trim or crop boundary by 9 mm; printed copy also needs the 9 mm inset. Independent restaging, off-center extraction, missing copy or breached protections fails. Cover and end-card placement are checked in the document and film rules.

Compare visible room relationships and perspective with workshop-plan.png, workshop-mark.png and the geometry and station records. Preserve the 6000 × 4000 mm room, north window at x 1600–4000 mm with center height 1400 mm, bench at x 1800–4200 and y 1200–2100 mm, and east cabinet at x 5200–5800 and y 800–2300 mm. Where visible, retain the west door, matte gray concrete floor and square dark walnut plaque with three equal vertical recessed slots above the cabinet. E01 must show Nora, window, bench and cabinet together from C2. All shots must have perspectives consistent with their recorded C1, C2 or C3 station and the 900 mm south-of-bench clearance. Framing may omit objects not required in a shot; relocated furniture, a wrong wall or incompatible perspective fails. Infer spatial compatibility rather than claiming exact measurements from uncalibrated photographs.

Require the visible ID/caption pairs D01/Blank, D02/Hollowing, D03/Oiled, D04/Hollowing, D05/Shaping, D06/Surface and D07/Oiled. Match each recorded subject and preserve the reference spoon's cherrywood, oval bowl, tapered rounded-end handle and dark curved grain streak from the left bowl rim toward the handle. Distinguish rough solid stock, partial hollowing, straight-knife handle shaping, dry fibers and the completed warm satin surface. D03 must show the entire finished spoon; D03, D06 and D07 must be square compositions. D03 and the visible portion in D07 must agree with the same finished object of 240 mm length and 65 mm bowl width; D07 may retain its specified close framing. Wrong labels, swapped stages, changed grain or inconsistent object proportions fails. Film evidence is checked separately.

Read the specification and compare the still photographs with its north-window direction, white-reflector fill, 2:1 lighting ratio and 5200 K white balance, also using the supplied empty-room atmosphere. Visible walls retain the warm gray #D8D2C8 plaster palette. Viewpoint, subject orientation and exposure choices may vary while maintaining a compatible light source, moderate contrast and color rendering. Conflicting shadows, a changed dominant source, strong unexplained color shifts or contradictory wall treatment fails. Judge visual compatibility rather than treating images as exact photometric measurements; the film is reviewed separately.

The story must communicate credible making through the required working views, contextual portraits and room photographs. Relevant details reveal wood fibers, tool wear and natural skin texture; grips, blade contact and workpiece placement are physically readable. Opening and inspection portraits may be posed as specified, and close details need not show the whole room. An incoherent maker-tool-bench relationship, implausible working gestures or smoothing that removes the requested material evidence fails.

The images must be compatible with one morning workshop session, preserving location, wardrobe and workpiece continuity while allowing the specified carving progression and tool return. Any visible clock, calendar or session notation must agree with the supplied date and time window. A second location, night-time transition or contradictory visible record fails. Do not require a timestamp or infer an exact date from daylight alone.

Match each delivered role to its applicable row in 03-shot-records.en.md and require the recorded subject, activity, workpiece stage and composition proportion. This includes seated handle shaping for P02, standing dry-bowl inspection for P03, blank selection for P04/E04, profile hollowing for P05, dry-grain inspection for P06, the oiled spoon toward the window for P07, cabinet context for E02, both knives being returned for E03, room-context hollowing for E05 and the oiled spoon resting on the bench beside Nora for E06 where those roles apply. Artistic framing may vary within the recorded proportion and required content. A substituted action, incorrect stage or wrong aspect relationship fails; portrait and environment images need not acquire printed labels unless required elsewhere.

Require a two-page process specification establishing the photographic approach and lighting setup before the still-image sequence. It must state the mapped north-window position, including its 1400 mm center height, white reflector, 2:1 lit-to-shadow ratio, 5200 K white balance and concrete selected shutter and aperture settings. The register must correctly associate all twenty-one applicable shot IDs with their proportions and recorded camera stations. Exposure choices may vary; missing settings, incorrect fixed facts, omitted shots or mismatched register entries fails. Treat precedence as the specification's process role and presentation placement rather than inferring creation timestamps.

Read presentation page 2 and require the same north-window position, 2:1 light ratio and 5200 K white balance established in the specification. Cross-check each reproduced still photograph's attached shot ID and proportion against the specification register and shot records. Equivalent notation such as 5200K is acceptable; misplaced page-two facts, missing labels, swapped IDs or incorrect proportions fails.

Visibly reuse the delivered specification and every one of the twenty-one still-image outputs. Scaling and presentation layout changes are acceptable if each actual source remains identifiable. Missing images, substituted versions of the scene, text-only references or omission of either opening treatment fails. Film-frame provenance is checked by whole-file manual review.

Require at least twelve pages, both required strings on the cover, the specification before the photographic story and three film-frame reproductions. In the expanded narrative, P04, E04 and D01 precede the hollowing images, including P05, E05, D02 and D04; P07, E06 and D07 follow them. The opening treatments may serve their designated introductory role. Any stated background, dimensions or session facts must agree with the client record. Missing frames, insufficient pages, absent cover copy or inverted required narrative groups fails.

Watch the complete film and verify its ten-second duration and the film record: Blank at 0–3 seconds, Hollowing at 3–7 seconds and Oiled at 7–10 seconds with closing title overlay. Require the approved Nora and wardrobe, both established knives, the same cherrywood spoon and persistent grain landmark through the three stages. Hollowing must use the walnut-handled hook knife in her right hand; the straight knife keeps its pale ash handle. Check C1/C3-compatible viewpoints, mapped workshop continuity, the specified north-window lighting, reflector-compatible 2:1 contrast and 5200 K appearance. The closing title must legibly include ALDER BENCH and A spoon, from blank to bowl. Compare the presentation's three claimed film frames with the actual video. Editing and shot lengths within the recorded passages may vary; wrong timing, reversed stages or handedness, changed identity or objects, absent closing copy or frames not found in the film fails.
